rows.finding: FULL TEXT states the finite-domain caveat: conditions can be satisfied and no pattern emerge when h is negative only between two discrete wavenumbers; the distance between wavenumbers shrinks as domain size grows. The ABSTRACT does not mention it.
rows.excerpt_short: "...h is not negative for any k within the discrete set of wavenumbers, and only takes a negative value in between two of these discrete wavenumbers."

rows.finding: FULL TEXT states: in a finite domain d > d_c alone does not guarantee pattern formation since the critical wavenumber might match no admissible mode for the domain and boundary conditions. The ABSTRACT does not mention it.
rows.excerpt_short: "In a finite domain, having d > d_c alone does not guarantee pattern formation since the critical wavenumber k_c might not match any admissible mode..."

rows.finding: Confirms: Table 1 reports case studies, not a controlled experiment; separating model from harness requires holding the model fixed and varying only the harness, left to future work.
rows.excerpt_short: "Table 1 reports case studies, not a controlled experiment."
